title: “The Argument” podcast, ad-free: Is the A.I. apocalypse coming for us all?
gist: Podcast-feed delivery page for the paid ad-free episode of 'The Argument' on whether an A.I. apocalypse is coming; the text contains no substantive argument, only pointers to the companion post 'The A.I. Apocalypse Canon and Why It Matters' and a list of recent episodes.

insights.claim: Slow Boring devoted a roughly 72-minute episode of 'The Argument' podcast to whether an A.I. apocalypse is coming, indicating A.I. catastrophic risk is a mainstream topic for centrist policy commentators.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Mainstreaming of A.I.-risk discourse raises odds of regulatory attention on frontier A.I.

insights.claim: The episode is paired with a written post, 'The A.I. Apocalypse Canon and Why It Matters', which hosts the transcript and discussion.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Pointer to the substantive companion piece for the actual argument.
insights.locator: If you’d rather stay on Substack

insights.claim: Recent episodes of the show covered the 'anti-social century' with Derek Thompson, hostility to elites, the crisis of global liberalism after 9/11, and whether a liberal center exists, showing a focus on social fragmentation and political realignment.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Signals the narratives centrist commentators are pushing ahead of the 2026 midterms.
